typed_core.name: form_variant
typed_core.why: IN-13 (rule reads it) — 'detect the income type'; also the disambiguator that says which box is the primary income (NEC->box 1, INT->box 1, DIV->box 1a, R->box 1)
typed_core.prompt_hint: The 1099 is a SERIES: NEC, INT, DIV, MISC, R (and others). Read the variant from the title and map the primary income box per variant

typed_core.name: tax_year
typed_core.why: IN-13 — the period the receipt covers; recency; the disambiguator beside the amount (a wage figure without its tax year can be misread)

typed_core.name: corrected_indicator
typed_core.why: processor — a CORRECTED 1099 supersedes the original figures; a rule/processor must know the amount is a restatement

typed_core.name: payer_name
typed_core.why: identity/attribution — who paid; third-party independence (IN-13 source of income)

typed_core.name: payer_tin
typed_core.why: PII (registered masked) — payer TIN/EIN; identity of the payer

typed_core.name: recipient_name
typed_core.why: identity — attaches the income to the borrower (IN-13 attribution)

typed_core.name: recipient_tin
typed_core.why: PII (registered raw) — recipient TIN/SSN; borrower match key (highly_restricted)

typed_core.name: recipient_address
typed_core.why: identity/occupancy match; PII — borrower address, must be typed or it lands unmasked in the catch-all

typed_core.name: income_amount
typed_core.why: IN-13 — the primary income box for the variant; the receipt amount IN-13 checks

typed_core.name: distribution_code
typed_core.why: IN-13 disambiguator — 1099-R box 7 code(s) tell a periodic/continuing pension (likely to continue) from a lump-sum/early distribution; without it IN-13 cannot judge continuance (flattened from distribution_codes string[])
typed_core.prompt_hint: For IN-13, the decision-relevant 1099 is usually the 1099-R (pension/retirement). Capture box 7 distribution code(s) — periodic vs lump-sum is what 'continuance' turns on

typed_core.name: taxable_amount_not_determined
typed_core.why: processor — 1099-R 'taxable amount not determined'; qualifies how much of the distribution counts

typed_core.name: account_number
typed_core.why: PII (restricted) — payer's account/annuity number; promote so it is masked rather than left unmasked in the catch-all; disambiguates which account/annuity

typed_core.name: second_tin_notice
typed_core.why: processor — flags a TIN mismatch the payer was warned about; authenticity signal

rejected.name: document_title, form_number, form_revision_date
rejected.reason: classification/version happen before extraction; form_variant identifies the form

rejected.name: document_issue_date, effective_date, expiration_date
rejected.reason: a 1099 reports a completed tax year; no effective/expiry; duplicates tax_year

rejected.name: statement_period_start/_end
rejected.reason: not a statement period; the tax year is the period

rejected.name: void_indicator
rejected.reason: marginal; a voided 1099 is rare and duplicates status — catch-all

rejected.name: box_values, state_local_values, distribution_codes (as list)
rejected.reason: the primary income + one distribution code are typed; the remaining boxes have no IN-13 consumer — catch-all (see Open questions)

encoding_variations: form_variant — read from the form title ('Form 1099-NEC', '1099-R', '1099-INT', '1099-DIV', '1099-MISC'). The variant governs which box is income; capture it verbatim

income_amount — the 'primary' box differs by variant (NEC box 1, INT box 1, DIV box 1a, R box 1 gross distribution, MISC the principal box present). The variant is its disambiguator; the tax year is a second disambiguator
distribution_code — 1099-R box 7 may carry one or two codes (e.g. 7=normal, 1=early, 4=death, 7D). Codes, not words, encode continuance
corrected_indicator / void_indicator — a checkbox at the top of the form; degrade to str

open_questions.q: Nest box_values or not? IN-13 needs only the primary income amount + distribution code (both typed)
options: leave other boxes to the catch-all now
add a flat-row box_values nested list (box_number, label, amount, source) for a future income/withholding rule
open_questions.recommendation: (a) now; revisit if a rule needs withholding or a non-primary box, since the catch-all is discarded at the snapshot boundary GEET'S DECISION (LP-438): BUILD IT — LP-437 made nested lists cheap (one declaration + the generic mechanism); the one-list-budget / defer / no-consumer concern is overturned. Build as flat_row; the per-rule consumer is separate follow-up.

open_questions.q: distribution_codes flattened to a single distribution_code str — box 7 usually holds 1-2 codes. Flattening to one str keeps the pair verbatim (e.g. '7D')
open_questions.recommendation: keep flattened str; confirm no case needs them as separate coded elements

open_questions.q: income_amount for MISC — MISC has several income boxes (rents box 1, other income box 3). The starter prompt takes 'the principal income box present'
open_questions.recommendation: keep that heuristic and record the box in the snippet as the disambiguator

notes: Tier 3 with one EXTRACT rule; IN-13 keys on form_variant + income_amount + distribution_code, the rest are identity/PII/disambiguators. 14 typed-core rows, below the 20-25 target, which is expected for a one-rule form.

box_values (object[]) is the catalog's repeating structure, but IN-13 needs only the single primary income amount plus the 1099-R distribution code — both typed. If a future rule needs withholding or every numbered box, box_values becomes the one flat-row nested list; today nesting it would spend ~5 sites of plumbing for no consumer.

PII: payer_tin already in _PII_FIELDS (masked); recipient_tin already in _PII_FIELDS (raw); recipient_address needs registration pre_masked false (borrower address; snapshot masks + salted match-hash); account_number needs registration pre_masked false (full account/annuity number; currently would land unmasked in the catch-all).
IRS box numbers: NEC box 1 = nonemployee comp; INT box 1 = interest; DIV box 1a = ordinary dividends; R box 1 = gross distribution, box 2a = taxable amount, box 7 = distribution code(s).
Money may include $/commas (parsed); TINs/SSNs as written. Never quote the full recipient TIN in reasoning.
distribution_code is flattened from a distribution_codes string[]; degraded_from recorded as 'object' to note the structural flatten (the field itself is a str).
